newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MAY 29.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The notorious November 17 terrorists returned with a venegeance yesterday after a hiatus of over a year, shooting down a young shipowner in the streets of Piraeus. Constantine Peratikos was shot seven times by three men as he left his office. Peratikos was the proprietor of the Elefsis Shipyards, which he abandoned in 1995 under the burden of overwhelming debts.

--The alarm bells have gone off at the economic crimes squad SDOE, which has issued a warning to merchants and businessmen to beware con artists posing as tax officials and extorting large amounts to "handle" any taxation affairs.

--Internal problems at Olympic Airways have grounded the national carrier and caused widespread disruption to flight scheduling. The problems with staffing have intensified with Greek stewards saying they will prevent the hiring of foreign cabin crews.

--Peratikos's murder was the 11th execution with the same .45 calibre pistol and the 21st since November 17's appearance in 1975. Previous statements by the group had mentioned the Elefsis Shipyards, purchased in 1992 by the Peratikos family.
--The secret behind the execution of Peratikos by terrorists yesterday lies in the 1992 purchase and 1995 reversal of the purchase of the Elefsis Shipyards.
--Former conservative prime minister Constantine Mitsotakis's recent self-critical comments on past political developments have brought a flurry of reactions from both sides of the political fence.
--Peratikos was unguarded despite repeated threats on his life from terrorists.
--An impoverished mother of three, due to be tried for pilfering food from the supermarket where she worked as a cleaner, killed herself while being held in detention.
--A spurned lover killed himself and his girlfriend's two children yesterday after forcing his way into the woman's suburban apartment. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
